overrides.why_this_special: July research shifted coding-agent evaluation toward sustained loops and streaming adaptation.

claims.text: LoopsBench defines a long-horizon coding-agent benchmark with 112 dependency-structured tasks spanning eight programming languages and nine domains.
AgentStream evaluates self-evolving agents under isolated, sequential, and interleaved streaming-task settings rather than only independent tasks.

limitations: Both benchmark designs and reported model rankings/results are author-reported; conclusions depend on the included harnesses, models, task sources, and scoring protocols.

artifact.canonical_name: July agent injection and MCP security research

overrides.why_this_special: July research exposed multiple agent attack surfaces beyond terminal prompt-injection success metrics.

claims.text: ContainmentBench argues that terminal attack success alone can hide materially different post-injection traces and evaluates containment, propagation, recovery, and authorized utility separately.
A separate July study evaluates stealthy concurrent audio prompt injection against multimodal agents, expanding the attack surface beyond text-only untrusted content.
Tool Specifications Matter reports that schema-formatted tool specifications can weaken refusal behavior and proposes SafeKeep as an inference-time mitigation.
Exposed by Design reports four July measurement runs of internet-facing MCP servers and a dynamic audit across multiple MCP-specific vulnerability classes.

limitations: Each result has a distinct threat model and evaluation setup; the papers should not be merged into a single universal 'agents are unsafe' claim.

overrides.why_this_special: July research converged on persistence, rollback, and provenance as controls for long-lived agent memory.

claims.text: MemSecBench tracks malicious memory content across persistence, downstream consequence, and repair rather than evaluating memory poisoning at a single point.
ChronoMem proposes semantic versioning/checkpoints and rollback for agent memory and reports integration with Google ADK.
Memory Provenance Laundering formalizes an authority-amplification failure during memory consolidation and proposes a provenance-aware non-amplification firewall.

limitations: These are research prototypes/benchmarks with author-reported evaluations; production effectiveness across arbitrary memory backends and agents is not independently established.

overrides.why_this_special: July systems work targeted KV reuse, sandbox cold starts, and repeated tokenization in long-running agents.

claims.text: AAFLOW+ treats reusable KV cache as a distributed workflow object for multi-agent pipelines rather than a request-local optimization.
SpecBox proposes speculative sandbox preallocation/prewarming to trade resource use against cold-start tail latency in sandboxed agent workloads.

TokTier proposes exact stateful CPU/GPU tokenization for append-heavy agent sessions, motivated by measurements showing repeated long-prefix tokenization can become a front-end bottleneck as prompt-cache hit rates rise.

limitations: The systems gains are author-reported and depend on analytical/microbenchmark assumptions, workload traces, serving stack, and hardware.

overrides.why_this_special: July serving releases concentrated on expert parallelism, Blackwell coverage, and MoE kernels.

claims.text: FlashInfer v0.6.15 shipped expert-parallel MoE support in the default install and expanded Blackwell-family serving coverage.
FlashInfer v0.6.16 followed with MegaMoE kernels, further Blackwell model coverage, an expanded unified MoE API, and distributed-serving changes including confidential-computing support.

limitations: Hardware/model support is highly GPU-generation-specific, and any throughput numbers in release notes are project benchmarks rather than general serving guarantees.

overrides.why_this_special: Major July 9 frontier-model family release followed by July efficiency/pricing updates.

claims.text: OpenAI launched the GPT-5.6 family for general availability on July 9, 2026 with Sol, Terra, and Luna tiers across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API.
The release introduced Programmatic Tool Calling in the Responses API and a multi-agent beta; OpenAI's `ultra` setting coordinates parallel agents for demanding tasks.
OpenAI later reduced GPT-5.6 Luna pricing by 80% and Terra pricing by 20% on July 30.
Performance-per-dollar and benchmark superiority claims in the launch and follow-up articles are OpenAI/vendor claims even when they reference third-party benchmarks.

limitations: Benchmark, efficiency, and estimated-cost comparisons are largely vendor-reported and depend on effort levels, harnesses, token usage, and pricing assumptions; they should not be flattened into a universal ranking.

overrides.why_this_special: July systems research addressed diffusion regional execution and MoE-aware speculative decoding.

claims.text: FlashDiff proposes regional execution and scheduling to reduce repeated full-region computation and communication overhead in diffusion-model serving.
EcoSpec proposes cost-aware speculative decoding for sparse MoE models by considering expert activation/scattering in addition to token acceptance likelihood.

limitations: Both are author-evaluated systems papers; reported gains depend on their selected models, hardware, workloads, and baselines.

overrides.why_this_special: Two substantial July releases changed speculative decoding and model-serving support.

claims.text: SGLang v0.5.15 made its Spec V2 path default and included production tuning for newer model/hardware combinations.
SGLang v0.5.16 introduced DSpark, a confidence-driven speculative-decoding algorithm that varies verification windows using draft confidence.

limitations: Reported throughput/TPS figures are project benchmarks under specific batch size, tensor-parallel, model, and GPU configurations.

overrides.why_this_special: Two substantial July releases changed the default dense-model execution path and frontier-model support.

claims.text: vLLM v0.25.0 made Model Runner V2 the default execution path for dense models and removed the legacy PagedAttention implementation.
vLLM v0.26.0 added broad new model-family support and expanded attention, speculative-decoding, KV-offload, and DeepSeek-V4-related optimizations.

limitations: Performance percentages in release notes are project measurements for specific kernels/models; integration support does not by itself prove model quality or availability outside vLLM.
